     invoice = _INVOICES.get(invoice_id)
+    if invoice is None:
+        return errors.problem(404, "Invoice not found", f"No invoice with id {invoice_id}")
     return jsonify(invoice.__dict__)

`GET /invoices/<id>` now returns a 404 when the invoice doesn't exist. Before this change, a missing ID made the handler crash on `None.__dict__`, which came back as a 500.

```python
invoice = _INVOICES.get(invoice_id)
if invoice is None:
    return errors.problem(404, "Invoice not found", f"No invoice with id {invoice_id}")
```

The 404 uses `errors.problem()` from `src/api/errors.py`, so the body is in the standard `application/problem+json` format. A project memory says all API endpoints must use that shared error format, because clients parse error bodies automatically. I imported it as `from src.api import errors`, the same `src.`-prefixed style the tests use.

I haven't run the endpoint: Flask isn't installed in this environment, so my smoke test failed on the import. The file does compile. There are no existing tests for the invoices API, and I didn't add one.
